content.title: About
content.content: Taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a soft flour tortilla, seasoned ground beef, and melted cheese. The tortilla provides a tender base, the beef adds a rich meaty flavor, and the cheese contributes a creamy note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flour tortillas originated in northern Mexico in the 19th century as an alternative to corn tortillas.
Tacos are often served with a variety of toppings: salsa, guacamole, onions, and cilantro.
In the United States, tacos became a popular fast‑food item after World War II when American soldiers brought the recipe back from Mexico.
Traditional Mexican tacos are usually cooked on an open flame, giving the meat a distinctive char.
There are over 100 taco variations, differing in meat type, sauces, and presentation.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground beef in tacos provides a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat supplies a notable amount of iron, supporting normal blood formation.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and cheese contain B12, B6, and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Complex carbs from tortilla
items.content: Flour tortillas provide sustained energy through complex carbohydrates.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Cheese and fatty beef can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt in the filling and sauces may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten in tortilla
items.content: Flour tortillas contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tacos hot, folding the tortilla in half and filling it with seasoned ground beef, shredded cheese, and preferred toppings such as salsa, guacamole, fresh onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. A dollop of sour cream or yogurt can add extra creaminess.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared tacos are best eaten immediately. If needed, store the cooked beef filling in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep tortillas in a dry, cool place at room temperature, and store cheese in the refrigerator wrapped in plastic.
